'''Goéry Delacôte''', ''[[Légion d'honneur]]'',<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012">{{cite web|title=Speech by HE Bernard Emié, French Ambassador to the United Kingdom at the ceremony to award the insignia of Officier in the Ordre national de la Légion d'Honneur to Goéry Delacôte, Chief Executive of the "At-Bristol" science centre|url=http://www.ambafrance-uk.org/IMG/pdf/Amba_S_13032012.pdf|work=Ambassador's Activities|publisher=French Embassy in the UK|access-date=8 June 2012}}</ref> is a French [[theoretical physicist]] and [[science educator]]. He has been involved with the direction of [[science centre]]s in Europe and the United States. He was instrumental in establishing the [[Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie]] in Paris, and was head of scientific information and communication at the [[Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]] (CNRS) for 10 years from 1982.

Delacôte founded the [[Exploradôme]] in Paris<ref name="businessweek">{{cite web|title=Goéry Delacôte: Executive Profile & Biography|url=http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=2309151&privcapId=2221131|archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20171013222730/http://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=2309151&privcapId=2221131|url-status=dead|archive-date=13 October 2017|work=[[Bloomberg Businessweek]]|access-date=6 June 2012}}</ref> and has held prominent posts at science centres in San Francisco, California and Bristol, England.<ref name="iop delacote 2006">{{cite web|last=Delacôte|first=Goéry|title=Once a physicist: Goéry Delacôte|url=http://www.tiptop.iop.org/index.cfm?action=summary&doc=19%2F12%2Fphwv19i12a51%40pwa-xml&qt=|work=Physics World|publisher=[[Institute of Physics]]|access-date=6 June 2012|date=December 2006}}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref name="bristol247 brown 2012">{{cite news|last=Brown |first=Christopher |title=At-Bristol announces new chief executive |url=http://www.bristol247.com/2012/01/10/at-bristol-announces-new-chief-executive-88448/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130118130929/http://www.bristol247.com/2012/01/10/at-bristol-announces-new-chief-executive-88448/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 January 2013 |access-date=6 June 2012 |newspaper=bristol247.com |date=10 January 2012 }}</ref>

== Biography ==

Delacôte's first name, Goéry, is possibly inspired by the founder of the commune of [[Épinal]]. The town is close to Delacôte's birthplace of [[Anould]].<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012" />

=== Education ===

At an early stage of his schooling, Delacôte [[grade skipping|skipped]] two grades. This encouraged his interest in physics, because he "wasn't mature enough to really appreciate the literature and poetry".<ref name="iop delacote 2006" /> He said that he became interested in physics because he considered mathematics to be too abstract,<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012" /><ref name="iop delacote 2006" /> and biology to be less scientific discipline.<ref name="iop delacote 2006" /> He studied at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] (ENS),<ref name="businessweek" /> with its highly regarded physics laboratories<ref name="iop delacote 2006" /> under [[Pierre Aigrain]].<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012" /> He refused to take the compulsory postgraduate teaching exam, in preference to further education and research.<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012" />

There, he gained his PhD in solid-state physics,<ref name="knowtex cocaud 2011">{{cite web|title=Rencontre avec Goéry Delacôte, directeur de @t Bristol|last=Cocaud|first=Camille|url=http://www.knowtex.com/blog/rencontre-avec-goery-delacote-directeur-de-t-bristol/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111126011023/http://www.knowtex.com/blog/rencontre-avec-goery-delacote-directeur-de-t-bristol/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=26 November 2011|work=knowtex blog|date=12 April 2012|access-date=6 June 2012}}</ref> after finding it difficult to choose between [[condensed matter physics|condensed matter]] and [[particle physics|particle]]/[[nuclear physics|nuclear]] (the two dominant areas at the time). He chose organic crystals as his research area because of a desire to help less developed nations: by his reasoning, condensed matter physics was the less expensive of the two.<ref name="iop delacote 2006" />

Delacôte helped organise a science [[summer school]] for Algerian students in 1962. He then undertook his doctoral research at the [[University of Algiers]], in association with the ENS<ref name="iop delacote 2006" /> and later taught at [[Paris Diderot University]].<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012" /> In 1969 he returned to the ENS, where he became a professor after completing his doctorate.<ref name="iop delacote 2006" />

=== Science centres ===
{{quote box
 |quote  = Money is our oxygen. Co-operation with the private sector is guided by financial considerations, but is not limited to this dimension. It is up to the partners to express what they want and what objectives they share clearly.
 |source = Goéry Delacôte, {{nowrap|May 2004}}<ref name="rtdinfo 2004">{{cite web|title=Science centres and museums - Showcasing science|url=http://ec.europa.eu/research/rtdinfo/41/print_article_933_en.html|work=RTDinfo|publisher=[[Europa (web portal)|Europa]]|access-date=6 June 2012}}</ref> 
 |width  = 40%
 |align  = right
 |qalign = right
 |quoted = 1
}}
Delacôte led a working group on new methods of teaching physical sciences in schools.<ref name="iop delacote 2006" /> He was approached to join [[Maurice Lévy (physicist)|Maurice Lévy]]'s team in 1979<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012" /> to help establish what was to become the [[Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie]]. In doing so, he visited major museums in the United States.<ref name="europusa 2001">{{cite web|last=Bronwyn|first=L|title=Goery Delacote, directeur de l'Exploratorium de San Francisco|url=http://www.europusa.com/node/552|work=europusa.com|access-date=6 June 2012|archive-date=22 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111222074600/http://www.europusa.com/node/552|url-status=dead}}</ref> His work began as a part-time job, with him eventually becoming chief scientist there. In 1982 he was made director of scientific and technical information of the [[Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique|CNRS]], creating the [[Institut de l'information scientifique et technique|INIST]] in 1988.<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012" /> His ten-year period there included founding a new national library for research, an agency for communicating scientists' research to the public<ref name="iop delacote 2006" /> and a partnership with [[Google]] to provide free access to {{nowrap|13 million}} bibliographical references.<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012" /> In 1985 he became board chairman and scientific director of the [[Institut national de recherche pédagogique]],<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012" /> where he remained until 1991.<ref name=exploratorium>{{cite web|title=Museum History: Dr. Goéry Delacôte; Executive Director, 1991–2005|url=http://www.exploratorium.edu/about/our_story/history/goery/|work=Exploratorium|publisher=[[Exploratorium]]|access-date=8 June 2012}}</ref>

Inspired by the success of San Francisco's [[Exploratorium]], Delacôte became friends with [[Frank Oppenheimer]]. Following Oppenheimer's death in 1985, he was headhunted<ref name="europusa 2001" /> to the Exploratorium, becoming executive director there from 1991 until 2005. During his tenure as executive director, Dr. Delacôte worked toward extending the reach of the museum through networking—increasing outreach, expanding teacher [[professional development]] programs, creating an expanded Web presence, and supporting the formation of museum partnerships in the U.S. and abroad.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.exploratorium.com/ | title=Redirection homepage | access-date=7 January 2014 | archive-date=7 January 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140107044545/http://exploratorium.com/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>  He founded the [[Exploradôme]] in Paris in 1998.<ref name="iop delacote 2006" />

From 2005 until 2012 he was Chief Executive of the [[At-Bristol]] science centre. His September 2005 move there came about for personal reasons, with his family being in London and France.<ref name="sfgate perlman 2005">{{cite news|last=Perlman|first=David|title=Exploratorium chief takes post in England|url=https://www.sfgate.com/science/article/SAN-FRANCISCO-Exploratorium-chief-takes-post-in-2668130.php|access-date=6 June 2012|newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=25 May 2005}}</ref><ref name="bristol-business fox-clinch 2012">{{cite news|last=Fox-Clinch|first=John|title=New chief executive will bring science and industry to At-Bristol|url=http://www.bristol-business.net/new-chief-executive-will-bring-science-and-industry-to-at-bristol/|access-date=6 June 2012|newspaper=bristol-business.net|date=20 January 2012}}</ref> In an interview in 2006, he said that he wanted to concentrate on "the quality of the exhibits and activities, and developing a network of science centres across the UK". He also said that he was disappointed with the level of English government funding for science centres, considering arrangements in Scotland and Wales to be better.<ref name="iop delacote 2006" /> His time in Bristol has been credited by the French Ambassador to the UK with giving the centre a "completely new lease of life", by assembling teams including scientists and the best exhibit designers.<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012" />

In 2011 Delacôte was appointed by [[Cambridge Science Centre]] as chairman, the intention being to open a science centre in Cambridge.<ref name="cambridge-news 2011">{{cite news|title=Science centre expert will help to guide fledgling group|url=http://www.cambridge-news.co.uk/Cambridge/Science-centre-expert-will-help-to-guide-fledgling-group-27092011.htm|access-date=6 June 2012|newspaper=[[Cambridge News]]|date=27 September 2011|archive-date=1 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120101023341/http://www.cambridge-news.co.uk/Cambridge/Science-centre-expert-will-help-to-guide-fledgling-group-27092011.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> Upon leaving At-Bristol in 2012, he expected to return to France to develop a network of science centres similar to the Exploradôme.<ref name="ambafrance-uk 2012" />
